deepdive.divline: - Dividend ₹7/share (70% on FV ₹10) — consistent payout policy driven by operating cash flow

profile.entities: HeidelbergCement India Ltd (this listco); parent group also building 3 MT integrated plant in Karnataka (outside listco) and owns Zuari Cement — eventual merger of all entities flagged ("timing issue", no timeline)
profile.mgmt: Joydeep Mukherjee (MD); Anil Sharma (CFO); Amit Angra (Head IR & SVP Finance)
profile.subseg: Cement (blended PPC/composite, premium trade products); geographies: Madhya Pradesh (Damoh/Imlai), UP (Jhansi), Central India core; small Karnataka (LBTT) grinding unit
profile.themes: GST rate cut on cement 28%→18% (demand tailwind); pet coke/fuel inflation from West Asia conflict; UP election-driven Central India cement demand

deepdive.sec: Cement — Central India (regional player, blended/low-carbon focus) — *hand-curated*

bull_bear.body:
- **Debt-free** (repaid ₹68.7cr interest-free loan in FY26); ₹403.7cr cash; negative net operating working capital.
- Dividend ₹7/share (70% on FV ₹10) — consistent payout policy driven by operating cash flow.
- Buyback suggested by retail investor; mgmt noncommittal ("will explore in management committee / Board").
bull_bear.title: Capital Allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Central India pricing weakness** persisting 3-4 quarters due to competitor capacity (JK expansion, UltraTech ramp, other new clinker lines); Dalmia/JP-asset 5 MT operationalizing from Q2 adds supply pressure. Mgmt expects parity to follow North India over 1 yr (no "islands of prosperity"); pre-monsoon prices stay soft.
- Fuel/petcoke inflation from West Asia conflict; currency depreciation (importer of fuel).
- Near-full capacity utilization caps volume upside until new capacity lands.
- El Niño/heat-wave → rural demand & food inflation.
- Approval risk: Gujarat EC and MP mine capacity approvals outside company control.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and measured. MD repeatedly insists cost push "always gets passed on, with a lag" and that larger players (150/180/100 MT) feel balance-sheet pain more, forcing industry pricing discipline. Bullish on UP election demand. Explicitly cautious / refused "crystal ball gazing" on structural pricing beyond cost-push pass-through, and declined to set timelines for Gujarat plant, MP mines, and Zuari merger. Some Q&A answers vague/evasive on exact numbers (clinker sales volume "difficult to share," blended Kcal cost "need to recheck").
bull_bear.title: Mgmt Tone

bull_bear.body:
- Volume growth (+8.8%) was partly engineered by **lowering clinker factor** (composite cement, −17% clinker) rather than adding clinker — i.e., grinding-side stretch, not capacity addition; gives only "1-2 years" headroom.
- Clinker debottlenecking physically done (3.1→3.23 MT) but **regulatory capacity uplift still pending** — installed vs approved capacity gap.
- Karnataka ~0.5 MT LBTT unit runs at low quantity; total company capacity is ~6.26 MT (not the 5.7-5.75 MT Central India figure analysts quote).
- Parent's 3 MT Karnataka integrated plant sits OUTSIDE the listco — future merger could transfer it in.
- FY EBITDA growth was input-cost-led, NOT price-led (price was a net drag) — margin quality depends on continued fuel optimization.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

business.body:
- ~97% of cement produced is blended (low-carbon); launched composite cement with ~17% lower clinker content, ramping up.
- **Premium products = 52% of trade volumes (+9% YoY)** — 3-yr premiumization strategy.
- Trade mix: **81% trade (retail) / 19% B2B**; ~45% volumes dispatched by road (+1% YoY).
- Clinker-to-cement (CC) ratio ~60-61%; targeting 50-100 bps reduction (down from 1.5-1.65 historically), freeing grinding headroom.
business.title: Segment

business.body:
- ⭐ Heidelberg itself a relative beneficiary of fuel inflation vs larger peers — its petcoke↔coal switching caps cost impact to ₹150/t vs industry ₹300-400/t.
- ✅ UP election spend → Central India cement demand beneficiaries (Heidelberg, JK Cement, UltraTech Central ops).
- Competitor capacity (JK, UltraTech, Dalmia/JP 5 MT) = pricing challenge for incumbents like Heidelberg.

---
business.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 EBITDA/ton ₹584 (+10% YoY); FY price drag −₹16/t offset by RM −₹11/t plus gains in power & fuel, freight, other.
- **Fuel mix flexibility:** petcoke earlier ~60-65%, cut by ~10% over last 2-3 months → coal up from ~30% to ~40%; petcoke now ~30% more expensive than coal on Kcal (petcoke ~₹2-2.25/Kcal vs coal ~₹1.5). Linkage coal sufficient; no open-market purchases of significance.
- **AFR (alt fuel) 11%** (+3% YoY); **non-grid power >50%** of FY; **green power >40%** (target modest increase beyond 40% in FY27/FY28).
- **Lead distance ~370-372 km** (FY26 & Q4 similar; +~5 km over 6 months — not material).
- Carbon <500 kg/ton cement; 4.8x water positive.
- **No imports of fuel/clinker** (mgmt corrected analyst's assumption — company does NOT import).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & Cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** FY26 volume +8.8% (3.05 MT clinker prod, ~95% util); EBITDA/ton ₹584 (+10% YoY, from ₹530); EBITDA +19.8%, PAT +25.5%; debt-free, ₹403.7cr cash; div ₹7/sh. Q4 a record 1.35 MT volume but QoQ gross price −₹105/t. Premium = 52% of trade (+9%). Khandwa ₹130cr blending unit (+0.4 MTPA) approved; won 2 MP limestone leases (167 MT). Capex guide ₹100cr FY27 / ₹120cr FY28. Guidance: Central India industry +7-7.5%; H1FY27 cost push ₹100-160/t to be passed on with lag. Pricing weak in Central India 3-4 qtrs; Gujarat plant & Zuari merger still no timeline.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Volume growth:** In line with Central India industry, which MD expects to grow **7-7.5%** this fiscal (ramping higher into UP elections / early CY). Heidelberg can't fully match industry as it's near full utilization; can sustain ~90% util FY27/FY28 on yearly basis (QoQ harder to predict).
- **EBITDA/ton:** No explicit forward target; FY26 exited at ₹584.
- **Pricing / cost push:** Industry talks of ₹300-400/t H1FY27 cost inflation (fuel + packaging); Heidelberg expects **only ₹100-160/t** impact (₹100-150 next qtr) due to fuel-mix flexibility (shift petcoke→coal). Confident of passing on the cost push "with a lag"; cautious that pre-monsoon pricing stays under "a little bit of pressure."
- **Capex (company-wide):** Sustaining capex ₹45-50cr/yr (~40% of annual depreciation). Khandwa blending unit ₹130cr split over FY27-FY28 (front-light, back-loaded). **Total capex ≈ ₹100cr FY27, ≈ ₹120cr FY28.**
- **Expansion timeline:** Khandwa unit completion within ~2 yrs (CT received). Gujarat plant (2.5-4 MT, not firmed) awaiting govt EC — not in hand. MP mines → "very firm plans," earlier than 4 yrs, no exact date.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- Central India demand outlook strong: monsoon dip then post-monsoon recovery into **UP elections** (highest cement-consuming state) — key demand impetus over next ~1 yr.
- Structural tailwinds: robust domestic consumption; **GST cut 28%→18%** on cement (prior year).
- Headwinds flagged: El Niño / heat wave risk to agri output, rural demand, food inflation (expected mitigated by monsoon); elevated headline inflation + currency depreciation (matters for an importer of fuel).
outlook.title: Demand / Pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Khandwa blending unit:** ₹130cr, +30-35k tons/month (~0.4 MTPA), serves a market Damoh can't reach; ~2 yr completion.
- **MP mining leases won (preferred bidder):** Kuria/Shivpur block ~350 ha = 62 MT limestone; second Shivpur block ~350 acres = 105 MT limestone — for "future expansions," details withheld. (167 MT cement-grade reserves total.)
- **Gujarat plant:** 2.5-4 MT, pending EC; +2.5-3 yrs to product after EC.
- **Group consolidation:** parent building 3 MT integrated Karnataka plant (outside listco); eventual merger of Zuari + Heidelberg + entities flagged — "timing issue," no timeline.
- Clinker debottlenecking (3.1→3.23 MT) done (capex complete); govt capacity-increase approval still pending.
outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

deepdive.thesis: Debt-free, cash-rich (₹403.7cr) Central-India regional cement player running ~90-95% utilization on ~6.26 MT total capacity. FY26 was a beat: volume +8.8%, EBITDA +19.8%, PAT +25.5%, EBITDA/ton up 10% to ₹584. Story now hinges on (a) running into a capacity wall (1-2 yrs of headroom, bought via clinker-factor reduction not new lines), (b) a small ₹130cr Khandwa blending unit (+0.4 MTPA by FY28) as the only near-term hard expansion, and (c) optionality from two newly-won MP limestone mining leases (167 MT reserves) + pending Gujarat EC + eventual Zuari/Karnataka group consolidation. Near-term risk: Central India pricing has been weak 3-4 quarters on competitor capacity additions (JK, UltraTech ramp), and ₹100-160/t fuel cost push in H1FY27 must be passed on with a lag.
